ei.subject: 2025년 6월 고3 모의고사
ei.title: Laura and Cathy at the Farmer's Market

fullPassage:
(A) "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be (a) her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables.

(B) Carrying the bags of peaches, Cathy came back and noticed Laura holding a box of blueberries and jars of jam. "Cathy, those peaches look delicious! I bought some blueberries. Would you like to go to my place and make blueberry pancakes together?" Laura asked. "Yes, that's an excellent idea!" replied Cathy happily. As they walked out of the market, Cathy thanked her friend for the special experience, saying "(b) I really love this place! Thank you for the wonderful day."

(C) Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me show you around. Are you ready?" Cathy answered excitedly, "Absolutely! I'm going to buy some fresh peaches!" The market was already crowded with people of all ages. "Cathy, you can taste the best of the season here," said Laura. Cathy smiled and began to look around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some. Curious to explore more, Cathy said, "While (c) you're buying jam, I'll look around the market and get some peaches."

(D) Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled heavenly. From a fruit stand, (d) she picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great choice because they're only here until this week. If you miss them now, (e) you'll have to wait another year for the season." Hearing that, Cathy said, "Oh, I'll get some more then! They're really cheap!" She bought two bags of peaches.

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in (A)[delight / despair]. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more (B)[common / rare], Cathy had never had a chance to buy (C)[freshly-picked / artificially-grown] fruits or vegetables.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 친구를 보고 기쁘게(delight) 달려갔고, 대도시에서는 대형마트가 더 흔했으며(common), 갓 수확한(freshly-picked) 과일을 살 기회가 없었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① delight — common — freshly-picked: 원문과 정확히 일치
❌ ② despair(절망)는 delight(기쁨)의 반의어
❌ ③ rare(드문)는 common(흔한)의 반의어
❌ ④ artificially-grown(인공 재배된)은 freshly-picked의 반의어
det.tip: delight(기쁨)↔despair(절망), common(흔한)↔rare(드문), freshly-picked(갓 수확한)↔artificially-grown(인공 재배된)

questions.passage: The market was already (A)[crowded / deserted] with people of all ages. "Cathy, you can taste the best of the season here," said Laura. Cathy smiled and began to look around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some. (B)[Curious / Reluctant] to explore more, Cathy said, "While you're buying jam, I'll look around the market and get some (C)[fresh / stale] peaches."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 시장은 모든 연령대의 사람들로 붐비고(crowded), 더 탐험하고 싶은 호기심(Curious)에, 신선한(fresh) 복숭아를 사겠다고 말했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ crowded — Curious — fresh: 원문과 일치
❌ ① deserted(텅 빈)는 crowded의 반의어
❌ ② Reluctant(꺼리는)는 Curious의 반의어
❌ ④ stale(신선하지 않은)는 fresh의 반의어
det.tip: crowded(붐비는)↔deserted(텅 빈), curious(호기심 있는)↔reluctant(꺼리는), fresh(신선한)↔stale(상한)

questions.passage: Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled (A)[heavenly / terrible]. From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, (B)[ripe / unripe] peaches. The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great choice because they're only here until this week. If you (C)[miss / catch] them now, you'll have to wait another year for the season."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 향기가 천상의(heavenly)였고, 잘 익은(ripe) 복숭아를 골랐으며, 지금 놓치면(miss) 내년까지 기다려야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② heavenly — ripe — miss: 원문과 일치
❌ ① unripe(덜 익은)는 ripe의 반의어 — 예쁘고 덜 익은 복숭아는 모순
❌ ③ terrible(끔찍한)은 heavenly의 반의어
❌ ④ catch(잡다)는 miss의 반의어 — 잡으면 기다릴 필요 없으므로 문맥 반대
det.tip: heavenly(천상의, 황홀한)↔terrible(끔찍한), ripe(잘 익은)↔unripe(덜 익은), miss(놓치다)↔catch(잡다)

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in ①<u>delight</u>. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first experience at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more ②<u>common</u>, Cathy had never had a ③<u>chance</u> to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables. Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me show you around." Cathy answered ④<u>reluctantly</u>, "Absolutely! I'm going to buy some fresh peaches!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: Cathy는 "Absolutely!"라고 신나게 대답했으므로 ④reluctantly(마지못해)는 부적절. 원문은 excitedly(신나서).
det.analysis:
❌ ④ reluctantly(마지못해) → 원문은 excitedly(신나서). "Absolutely!"라는 답변과 모순
✅ ① delight(기쁨): 친구를 보고 기뻐서 달려감 — 적절
✅ ② common(흔한): 대도시에는 대형마트가 흔하다 — 적절
✅ ③ chance(기회): 신선한 과일을 살 기회가 없었다 — 적절
det.tip: excitedly(신나서)↔reluctantly(마지못해): 감정과 행동의 일치 여부를 확인

questions.passage: The market was already crowded with people of all ages. Cathy smiled and began to look around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some. Curious to explore more, Cathy said she would look around. Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to ①<u>search</u> for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled ②<u>heavenly</u>. From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, ③<u>ripe</u> peaches. The fruit seller told her the peaches were a great choice because they were ④<u>permanent</u> — only here until this week.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 복숭아가 이번 주까지만 있다는 것은 한정적이라는 뜻이므로 ①permanent(영구적인)는 부적절. 문맥상 limited(한정적인)이 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ ripe(잘 익은): 아름답고 잘 익은 복숭아 — 적절
✅ ① search(찾다): 복숭아를 찾기 시작했다 — 적절
✅ ② heavenly(천상의): 꽃과 비누 향기가 황홀하다 — 적절
❌ ④ permanent(영구적인) → '이번 주까지만'이라는 문맥과 모순. 한시적 판매임
det.tip: permanent(영구적인)↔temporary(일시적인): '이번 주까지만' = temporary/limited

questions.passage: Carrying the bags of peaches, Cathy came back and noticed Laura holding a box of blueberries and jars of jam. "Cathy, those peaches look ①<u>delicious</u>! I bought some blueberries. Would you like to go to my place and make blueberry pancakes together?" Laura asked. "Yes, that's an excellent idea!" replied Cathy ②<u>happily</u>. As they walked out of the market, Cathy thanked her friend for the ③<u>special</u> experience, saying "I really love this place! Thank you for the ④<u>dreadful</u> day."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말 중, 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: Cathy가 "I really love this place!"라고 했으므로 ④dreadful(끔찍한)은 부적절. 원문은 wonderful(멋진).
det.analysis:
❌ ④ dreadful(끔찍한) → 원문은 wonderful(멋진). 장소를 사랑한다며 끔찍한 날이라 하면 모순
✅ ① delicious(맛있는): 복숭아가 맛있어 보인다 — 적절
✅ ② happily(행복하게): 훌륭한 아이디어라며 행복하게 답함 — 적절
✅ ③ special(특별한): 특별한 경험에 감사 — 적절
det.tip: wonderful(멋진)↔dreadful(끔찍한): 감정의 방향이 일치하는지 확인. love + wonderful = 긍정 일치

questions.passage: "Hi! I'm over here!" shouted Laura, waving brightly at Cathy at the entrance of Darlingdale Farmer's Market. Seeing her friend, Cathy rushed over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town, and this was going to be her first __________ at a real farmer's market. Born and raised in a big city, where large supermarkets were more common, Cathy had never had a chance to buy freshly-picked fruits or vegetables.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 농산물 직거래 시장에서의 첫 경험(experience)이 될 것이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ experience(경험): 원문 'first experience at a real farmer's market'
❌ ① complaint(불만): 기대하며 가는 상황과 부적합
❌ ② mistake(실수): 문맥상 실수와 무관
❌ ③ failure(실패): 기대감이 있는 상황과 반대
det.tip: experience: 경험. first experience = 첫 경험. 긍정적 기대를 나타내는 문맥

questions.passage: Entering the market, Laura said, "Let me show you around. Are you ready?" Cathy answered excitedly, "Absolutely! I'm going to buy some fresh peaches!" The market was already crowded with people of all ages. "Cathy, you can taste the best of the season here," said Laura. Cathy smiled and began to look around. Meanwhile, Laura found some strawberry jam for sale. She walked over to buy some. __________ to explore more, Cathy said, "While you're buying jam, I'll look around the market and get some peaches."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 더 많이 탐험하고 싶은 호기심(Curious)에 시장을 둘러보겠다고 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① Curious(호기심 있는): 원문 'Curious to explore more' — 적극적 탐색 의지
❌ ② Afraid(두려운): 시장에서 두렵다는 문맥 아님
❌ ③ Unwilling(내키지 않는): 직접 둘러보겠다며 적극적이므로 반대
❌ ④ Hesitant(망설이는): "I'll look around"이라는 적극적 발언과 모순
det.tip: Curious(호기심 있는): curious to V = ~하고 싶은 호기심에. 긍정적 탐색 의지 표현

questions.passage: Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled heavenly. From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great choice because they're only here until this week. If you miss them now, you'll have to wait another year for the __________." Hearing that, Cathy said, "Oh, I'll get some more then! They're really cheap!"
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 제철 과일이라 놓치면 내년 시즌(season)까지 기다려야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ season(시즌, 제철): 원문 'wait another year for the season' — 제철 복숭아
❌ ① market(시장): 시장은 매주 열리므로 1년을 기다릴 이유 없음
❌ ② discount(할인): 할인과 무관한 문맥
❌ ④ delivery(배달): 농산물 직거래 시장에서 배달은 부적합
det.tip: season: 제철, 시즌. 과일의 season = 그 과일이 나오는 시기. 복숭아 시즌 = 여름

questions.passage: Seeing her friend, Cathy <u>rushed</u> over in delight. Cathy had recently moved into Laura's town.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 rushed의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: rushed는 '급히 달려갔다'라는 뜻으로, hurried(서둘렀다)와 가장 가깝다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② hurried(서둘렀다): rushed의 동의어
❌ ① strolled(거닐었다): 천천히 걷는 것 — 반대
❌ ③ crawled(기어갔다): 속도가 매우 느림
❌ ④ wandered(배회했다): 목적 없이 돌아다님
det.tip: rush = hurry = 서두르다, 급히 가다. rush over = 급히 달려가다

questions.passage: The market was already <u>crowded</u> with people of all ages. "Cathy, you can taste the best of the season here," said Laura.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 crowded의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: crowded는 '붐비는, 사람이 가득한'이라는 뜻으로, packed(꽉 찬)와 가장 가깝다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① packed(꽉 찬): crowded의 동의어
❌ ② empty(비어 있는): crowded의 반의어
❌ ③ quiet(조용한): 사람이 많으면 조용하지 않음
❌ ④ decorated(장식된): 사람이 많은 것과 무관
det.tip: crowded = packed = 붐비는. be crowded with = ~으로 가득 차다

questions.passage: Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled <u>heavenly</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 heavenly의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: heavenly는 '천상의, 황홀한'이라는 뜻으로, wonderfully(훌륭하게)와 가장 가깝다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ wonderfully(훌륭하게, 놀랍도록): heavenly의 동의어 — 향기가 아주 좋다
❌ ① faintly(희미하게): 향기의 강도를 나타내지만 heavenly의 의미 아님
❌ ② unpleasantly(불쾌하게): heavenly의 반의어
❌ ③ ordinarily(평범하게): heavenly는 특별한 느낌
det.tip: heavenly: 천상의, 황홀한. smell heavenly = 천상의 향기가 나다 = 아주 좋은 냄새

questions.passage: From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, <u>ripe</u> peaches. The fruit seller told her they were a great choice.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ripe의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.korean: ripe는 '잘 익은'이라는 뜻으로, unripe(덜 익은)가 반의어.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ unripe(덜 익은): ripe의 반의어
❌ ① mature(성숙한): ripe와 유사어
❌ ② fresh(신선한): 잘 익은 것과 신선한 것은 다른 개념
❌ ④ juicy(즙이 많은): ripe와 관련 속성이지 반의어 아님
det.tip: ripe(잘 익은)↔unripe(덜 익은). un- 접두사 = ~하지 않은

questions.passage: "Yes, that's an excellent idea!" replied Cathy happily. As they walked out of the market, Cathy thanked her friend for the <u>special</u> experience, saying "I really love this place!"
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 special의 의미와 가장 반대되는 것은?

det.korean: special은 '특별한'이라는 뜻으로, ordinary(평범한)가 반의어.
det.analysis:
✅ ② ordinary(평범한): special의 반의어
❌ ① unique(독특한): special과 유사어
❌ ③ memorable(기억에 남는): special과 유사어
❌ ④ remarkable(주목할 만한): special과 유사어
det.tip: special(특별한)↔ordinary(평범한). 오답이 모두 special의 유사어라서 혼동 유발

questions.passage:
(A) From a fruit stand, she picked out some beautiful, ripe peaches. The fruit seller told her, "Those peaches are a great <u>choice</u>."

(B) Students have no <u>choice</u> but to follow the school rules strictly.
questions.stem: (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 choice의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 복숭아가 훌륭한 선택한 것(choice)이다. (B) 학생들은 선택의 여지(choice)가 없다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 선택한 것 — 선택의 여지: (A) a great choice = 훌륭한 선택, (B) have no choice = 선택의 여지가 없다
❌ ② 의미 순서가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (B)의 choice는 '결정'이 아닌 '선택의 여지'
❌ ④ (A)의 choice는 '결정'이 아닌 '선택한 것'
det.tip: choice: ① 선택한 것(a great choice = 좋은 선택) ② 선택의 여지(no choice = 선택의 여지 없음)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a feeling of great pleasure and happiness"

det.korean: '큰 기쁨과 행복의 감정' = delight(기쁨).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ delight(기쁨): 정의와 정확히 일치
❌ ① despair(절망): 기쁨의 반대 감정
❌ ② anxiety(불안): 기쁨과 다른 감정
❌ ④ frustration(좌절): 기쁨과 반대 감정
det.tip: delight: 기쁨, 즐거움. in delight = 기뻐하며. to one's delight = ~가 기뻐하게도

questions.passage: Cathy answered __________ (excite), "Absolutely! I'm going to buy some fresh peaches!"
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 동사 answered를 수식하는 부사 형태 excitedly(신나서)로 변환.
det.analysis: excite(흥분시키다) → excited(흥분한, 형용사) → excitedly(흥분하여, 부사). 동사 수식이므로 부사 필요.
det.tip: excite → excited(형용사) → excitedly(부사). -ly 접미사로 부사화. cf. happy → happily

questions.passage: Wandering away from Laura, Cathy began to search for peaches. Cathy walked past booths of fresh flowers and hand-made soaps, which smelled __________ (heaven).
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 감각동사 smelled 뒤에 보어로 형용사 heavenly(천상의)가 필요.
det.analysis: heaven(천국, 명사) → heavenly(천상의, 형용사). 감각동사(smell) + 형용사 보어 구조.
det.tip: heaven(명사) → heavenly(형용사). -ly가 붙어도 부사가 아닌 형용사인 경우: friendly, lovely, heavenly, costly

questions.passage: Carrying the bags of peaches, Cathy came back and noticed Laura holding a box of blueberries and jars of jam. "Cathy, those peaches look delicious! I bought some blueberries. Would you like to go to my place and make blueberry pancakes together?" Laura asked. "Yes, that's an excellent idea!" replied Cathy happily. As they walked out of the market, Cathy thanked her friend for the special experience, saying "__________"
